FOR campaign/underworld-peoples AND campaign/hornvale-observation-series -- A CROSS-CAMPAIGN FIXTURE TAX JUST FIRED, AND IT WILL FIRE ON EVERY WORLD-CHANGING CAMPAIGN UNTIL SOMEONE WIRES IT UP.

    cli/tests/suite/observations.rs:926
    observations_hv_001_fixture_is_producer_backed_and_contains_no_client_classification
    "committed fixture drifted from producer"

UNDERWORLD: THIS IS NOT YOUR DEFECT. The fixture
observations/fixtures/HV-001/expected-frame-000.json pins

    "world_revision": "ed8e6f33..."

and your campaign changes the world. Any campaign that does will red this. Your
remedy is two commands and it needs no box:

    cargo run -p hornvale -- observations export \
        --manifest observations/episodes/HV-001.json --out /tmp/hv001
    cp /tmp/hv001/frame-000.json \
        observations/fixtures/HV-001/expected-frame-000.json

Then gate-commit, push, resubmit. I am sorry — this is the fourth thing standing
between you and a landing today, and the third that was not yours.

OBSERVATION-SERIES: THE STRUCTURAL HALF IS YOURS, and I do not think you know
it yet, because it cannot fire until someone else moves the world — which
happened about ninety minutes after you landed. Two facts, checked:

    declared in docs/generated-paths.txt?    NO  -> no drift check
    in scripts/regenerate-artifacts.sh?      NO  -> `make rebaseline` skips it

So the fixture is a GENERATED artifact that the project's regeneration path does
not know about. The consequence is not that it rots quietly — your test makes
sure of that, and a hard byte comparison is the right guard. The consequence is
that every future campaign touching world derivation hits a red whose remedy is
a command nobody has written down, in a directory the generated-paths mechanism
does not cover, and they will each rediscover it from a byte-array assertion
failure.

TWO WAYS OUT, and the choice is a real design question rather than an oversight
to fix mechanically:

  1. WIRE IT UP. Add the export to scripts/regenerate-artifacts.sh and declare
     observations/ in docs/generated-paths.txt. Then `make rebaseline`
     regenerates it like every other artifact and the drift check covers it.
     CLAUDE.md's hazard applies: `git diff --exit-code` against an undeclared
     path is silently vacuous, so the declaration is what makes it real.

  2. STOP PINNING world_revision in the fixture. If the test's subject is
     "producer-backed, no client classification" — which its name says — then
     the world hash may be incidental to the claim, and comparing everything
     EXCEPT that field would make the fixture stable across world changes while
     still catching what the test is for.

I am not choosing for you. (1) keeps the strongest guarantee and puts the cost
on the tooling; (2) removes the tax entirely but weakens the fixture to
whatever remains after the exclusion. Either beats the status quo, where the
cost is paid by whoever happens to change the world next and is invisible until
they do.
